name: SS Umbria

sources.title: SS Umbria — built 1912 in Hamburg as Bahía Blanca: length 154.9 m, beam 18.1 m, twin screws; scuttled at Wingate Reef with about 6,000 t of bombs, detonators, cement and three Fiat 1100 cars; lies on her port side, at most 38 m
Umbria (Schiff, 1912) — Reiherstieg yard, 155.45 m overall, two masts; the starboard side just under the surface with the davits standing out of it

Mar Rosso — Umbria dive plan: lying on the port side, hull intact, four davits above the starboard side, the funnel on the bottom, two lifeboats at about 35 m, port propeller half buried, port anchor chain out, the holds (bombs aft, cement and wine, the Fiat cars on the starboard side aft of the superstructure)
Blue Force Fleet — the Umbria wreck: from about 5 to 33 m, starboard propeller at about 18 m, corals, sponges and fish

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q2478173_umbria.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. The hull whole, lying on her port side (about 75°, approximate) with the holds open: tyres and wire coils in hold 1, cement, wine and bombs in hold 2, the three Fiat 1100 'Lunga' cars on the starboard side of the 'tween deck of hold 3 with building material, bombs tier upon tier in holds 4 and 5; the passenger decks, bridge and davits on the central island; the funnel fallen and lying on the sand, the masts broken off and lying beside her, two lifeboats on the bottom near the stern, the port anchor chain out, bombs, crates and bottles spilt from the holds; twin propellers (the port one half buried) and the rudder; Red Sea corals and fish. The real wreck rests on the slope of Wingate Reef (about 30-38 m at the deep side, the starboard side a few metres under the surface); on a flat seabed she stands lower. Heading (not published: 0), colours, the stowage of the cargo and the place of the masts and boats are approximate. model_built.glb: the ship as she sailed as Umbria, before 1940.
